study_identification_part.si4_title: Dissecting task-based fMRI activity using normative modelling: an application to the Emotional Face Matching Task

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: Large-scale normative models of task-evoked fMRI activation (EFMT) are built to bind heterogeneous datasets to a common reference, quantify individual deviations, and relate them to transdiagnostic symptom domains; then applied to a naturalistic clinical cohort.

rci8_quality_checking.supporting_text: Participants were excluded if their mean relative RMS was greater than 0.5 mm ... we performed targeted quality control for this extended region ... selected the first 5000 participants ... additional out-of-sample/unseen 5000 UK Biobank participants

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Sparse CCA relating whole-brain (unthresholded) deviation maps to transdiagnostic functional domain factor loadings (negative valence, cognitive function, social processes, arousal/inhibition); 10-fold 70/30 splits; permutation testing; also voxel-wise case–control comparisons.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Patients show a higher frequency of extreme deviations for faces>shapes with heterogeneous spatial distribution; faces>baseline models relate more strongly to transdiagnostic functioning; normative deviations predict functional domains via SCCA, while diagnosis labels show little association.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Reference models achieved good test-set EV (up to ~0.525) in task-activated regions with acceptable skew/kurtosis; patients exhibited more frequent extreme deviations (|Z|>2.6) particularly for faces>shapes; SCCA yielded mean test-split r=0.224 (faces>shapes) and r=0.180 (faces>baseline), both p<0.001 (permutation). Additional out-of-sample validation on 5,000 UKB participants reproduced key metrics; test–retest showed stability across ~95% of the brain, strongest in visual regions; deviations in vmPFC are sensitive to signal dropout.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Model includes acquisition and task parameters (TR, multiband, volumes, blocks, instructions), site as covariate; provides structure coefficients for interpretability; compares warped (non-Gaussian) vs Gaussian BLR (retains Gaussian due to comparable fit); produces normative probability maps and total deviation counts; releases code and numerical source data (Zenodo).

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Cross-sectional design and general test–retest reliability limitations of task fMRI; under-representation of mid-adulthood (ages ~37–46) in the reference sample; variability and signal dropout in vmPFC influencing deviation metrics; heterogeneity in task implementations and acquisition across sites, though modelled.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: Contrasts modelled: faces>shapes and faces>baseline. Train/test splits were stratified by site. Supplementary materials include targeted vmPFC coverage QC for UKB and an additional out-of-sample validation on 5,000 UKB participants. Clinical application used MIND-Set; SCCA analyses performed with regularisation (10%) and 1000-fold permutation tests.
